name: Recommended mix: Cover crop – sunflower – vetch – sorghum – millet
description: Cover in both winters with drought-tolerant summer crops.
rule_ids: seleccion:mejor de 3 variantes mixtas con tus prioridades
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
obtain cover-crop seed and budget for planting and termination costs

name: Sorghum – oats – sunflower – vetch – millet
description: Five crops from three families, with short, drought-tolerant cycles; the oat green forage brings in livestock.
management: plan five different crops (planting, inputs and machinery)

name: Conservative: Grass cover crop – Sorghum – Oats – Sunflower
description: Keeps the base of the current rotation with minimal changes (grass cover crop in the winter of year 1).
management: terminate the cover crop in August so it does not use the fallow's water

name: Peanut – late corn – sunflower
description: It prioritizes high relative-income crops adapted to sandy soils (peanut) and plants corn late to avoid drought at flowering.
management: secure a sales contract for the peanut
cover the soil after peanut lifting, which leaves it very exposed to erosion

name: Sorghum – sunflower – millet with long fallows
description: It uses the catalog's most drought-tolerant summer crops, one with a very short cycle, and leaves long fallows to store water in the soil profile.
management: control weeds during the fallow so they don't use the stored water

name: Perennial pasture (3 years) – cover crop – sorghum
description: Crop-livestock rotation: the perennial pasture covers the soil year-round and rebuilds organic matter; when it is broken up, sorghum uses the released nitrogen.
management: own livestock or forage sales so the pasture generates income
terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
